newsitem.title: CHINA: China to give N.Korea 80,000 tonnes of grain.
newsitem.headline: China to give N.Korea 80,000 tonnes of grain.

text.p: China said on Tuesday it was donating a further 80,000 tonnes of grain to famine-stricken North Korea due to its traditional friendship with its socialist neighbour and on humanitarian grounds.

"Proceeding from the traditional relations between the peoples of the two countries and from humanitarian reasons, the Chinese government has decided to provide aid again," the Xinhua news agency said.
"This decision reflects the Chinese government's consistent stand and desire to treasure and actively develop Sino-Korean traditional friendly relations," Xinhua said.
The latest shipment would total 80,000 tonnes, most of it expected to be corn, it said.
China had informed North Korea of its decision and Pyongyang "expressed its heartfelt gratitude toward the Chinese government's friendly measure", Xinhua said.
North Korea, hit by two years of floods and failed harvests in 1995 and 1996, is on the brink of starvation, international aid workers say.
"The Chinese government and the people...have felt sympathy for the people of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea and offered help several times," Xinhua said.
In April, China said it would donate 70,000 tonnes of grain to North Korea to help its communist neighbour overcome severe food shortages, and it has already shipped all the corn.
The U.N. World Food Programme has appealed for $95.5 million for 200,000 tonnes of food for North Korea, well short of what aid workers say is needed to stave off famine.

Pyongyang has demanded substantial food aid before it will join talks between the two Koreas, the United States and China aimed at securing a lasting peace to replace a truce that ended the 1950-53 Korean war.
Top U.S. defence officials have cautioned against rushing to help North Korea, saying the nation was on a war footing despite its appeals for food to avert famine.
China fought with North Korea during the Korean war, but it has been forced to balance ties with its communist ally against its growing friendship for the capitalist South.
China has an abundant supply of corn, which would make up the bulk of the grain it would send to North Korea, officials said.
"Most of it will be corn...a small part will be rice," a spokesman for the Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation said.
"We still have to discuss the date of delivery," the spokesman said. He declined to provide further details.
